title: Memory zeroization
description: Cryptographic keys and secrets must be wiped from RAM the moment they're no longer needed — memset isn't enough (compilers optimize it away). Secure zeroization uses volatile writes or dedicated functions (explicit_bzero, SecureZeroMemory) that the compiler can't elide, ensuring secrets don't linger in memory for the next process to read.
method: Use explicit_bzero / SecureZeroMemory / volatile memset; wipe on all exit paths including errors; verify with memory scans in test.
usage: Zeroize keys on every exit path; audit for elided memsets; test with memory dumps.

demo.code:
import ctypes
buf = ctypes.create_string_buffer(b'secret-key-123')
ctypes.memset(buf, 0, len(buf.raw))
print('buffer zeroized:', buf.raw == b'\x00' * len(buf.raw))

title: TTL-based auto-expiry
description: Ephemeral data should die on schedule: TTLs on cache entries, self-destructing messages, auto-expiring tokens. The system, not human discipline, enforces deletion — data that can't linger because its lifetime is structural, not procedural.
method: Set TTLs at creation; enforce expiry in the storage layer; sweep expired data on schedule; log deletions.
usage: Default to short TTLs for sensitive temporaries; make 'forever' require justification.

demo.code:
import time
cache = {'token': (12345, time.time() + 300)}
val, exp = cache['token']
print('token valid:', time.time() < exp, '(auto-expires in 5 min)')

title: Forensic recovery resistance
description: Against forensic recovery, deletion must consider remapped sectors, wear leveling, and filesystem journals — all places 'deleted' bytes survive. Resistance means layered deletion (overwrite + crypto-shred + secure erase) matched to the medium, verified by attempting recovery in test.
method: Layer techniques per medium; attempt forensic recovery in test; close the gaps the recovery finds.
usage: Test deletion by trying to recover; assume the adversary has your test lab's tools.

demo.code:
print('deletion test: forensic scan of wiped drive')
print('recovered: 0 sensitive bytes -> RESISTANT')

title: Clipboard and UI residue clearing
description: Copied passwords linger in clipboards; secrets render in UI fields that screenshots capture. Sanitization clears clipboards after timeout, masks secret fields, and excludes them from screenshots and accessibility trees — the ephemeral data users handle directly.
method: Clear clipboard after N seconds; mask secret inputs; exclude from screenshots; limit accessibility exposure.
usage: Auto-clear sensitive clipboards; mask by default; test the screenshot path.

demo.code:
print('password copied -> clipboard auto-clears in 30s')
print('secret field: masked, FLAG_SECURE (excluded from screenshots)')

title: Ephemeral key exchange (PFS)
description: Perfect forward secrecy uses ephemeral keys per session (ECDHE): even if the long-term key is later compromised, past sessions stay secret because their keys were ephemeral and destroyed. PFS is sanitization built into the protocol — session data self-destructs by design.
method: ECDHE key exchange per session; destroy ephemeral keys after use; never log session keys.
usage: Require PFS cipher suites; verify ephemeral keys are actually destroyed.

demo.code:
print('session: ECDHE ephemeral keys -> destroyed after handshake')
print('long-term key later stolen: past sessions STILL SECRET (PFS)')

title: Data retention policies
description: The policy layer: what data lives how long, who approves exceptions, and how deletion is verified. Retention schedules (30 days for logs, 7 years for financials) plus automated enforcement turn 'delete old data' from intention into operation — sanitization at organizational scale.
method: Define retention per data class; enforce automatically; approve exceptions explicitly; audit compliance.
usage: Write the schedule down; automate enforcement; audit exceptions.

demo.code:
policy = {'debug logs': 30, 'access logs': 90, 'financials': 2555}  # days
print('retention schedule:', policy)
print('enforcement: auto-delete on expiry, exceptions need approval')

title: Log sanitization
description: Logs are where secrets go to live forever: passwords in URLs, tokens in headers, PII in debug output. Sanitization means structured logging with field-level redaction — secrets never enter the log pipeline, and patterns (credit cards, tokens) are scrubbed even from free text.
method: Structured logs; redactlist for sensitive fields; regex scrubbing for free text; review log samples for leaks.
usage: Redact at the logging call site; scrub defensively downstream; audit samples regularly.

demo.code:
import re
log = 'user login token=abc123-secret'
clean = re.sub(r'token=\S+', 'token=[REDACTED]', log)
print('sanitized log:', clean)

title: Swap and hibernation protection
description: Secrets in RAM can leak to disk via swap or hibernation files. Protection means locking sensitive pages (mlock/VirtualLock) so they never swap, and encrypting hibernation images — defense for the data's entire lifetime, including when the machine sleeps.
method: mlock sensitive buffers; encrypt swap or disable it for secret-handling processes; encrypt hibernation images.
usage: Lock key material in RAM; treat hibernation files as sensitive; audit swap configuration.

demo.code:
print('mlock(key_buffer): pages locked, never swapped')
print('hibernation image: encrypted -> secrets safe while asleep')
